CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Councilmember Ramirez welcomed all in attendance; encouraged residents to contact
City Council with any questions or concerns; invited all to attend National Night Out
August 5, at Norwalk Park; and shared that the Senior Center will be available as a
Cooling Center throughout the week and weekend. Councilmember Valencia reported
on her attendance at the Summer Concert; invited residents to attend the Summer
Concert & National Night Out event; announced the upcoming Southeast Water Coalition
meeting; and welcomed all back to school. Vice Mayor Rios reported on her attendance
at the Community Clean Up, the Bark and Brews event, Dream Big Project 8th Annual
Scholarship Awards Celebration, Soroptimist’s Quarter Mania, and Milagro’s Cinema
Screening; and invited all to attend Ice Cream with a Cop, August 5, at Target 12051
Imperial Highway. Mayor Perez recognized former Mayor Bob Arthur in attendance;
reported on her attendance at the Annual Joint Powers Insurance Authority Board of
Directors Meeting, the Soroptimist Quarter Mania event, Sal’s Psychiatry Services Ribbon
Cutting Ceremony; announced the City bulletins were distributed and highlighted
upcoming events; shared she will not be seeking reelection and thanked the community,
residents, businesses, and staff for a successful and productive nine years.

Gomez shared resources available to residents for those impacted by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement.

improvement projects funded through the California Department of Transportation's (Caltrans)
Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Cycles 6, 7, and 8. These projects support the
City's ongoing efforts to improve roadway safety, enhance accessibility, and modernize traffic
infrastructure by upgrading traffic signal hardware, optimizing signal timing coordination,
installing pedestrian countdown signal heads, reconstructing Americans with Disabilities Act
curb ramps, and improving roadway signage and striping.

The original Agreement with Avant-Garde was approved for a total amount of $201,139. As the
projects are federally funded, they require strict compliance with Caltrans and federal
requirements throughout project delivery. Avant-Garde provides specialized expertise in
managing these complex administrative requirements, including preparing and submitting
authorization requests, coordinating required documentation, administering reimbursement
requests for eligible project costs, and preparing final project closeout packages in accordance
with Caltrans requirements. These services help ensure the City remains eligible for federal
reimbursement, maintains compliance with grant requirements, and minimizes the administrative
burden on City staff.

Background:

In 2011, a group of cities/agencies, also known as watershed “Permittees,” including the City of
Norwalk created a Technical Committee to prepare an Implementation Plan, Monitoring Plan,
and special studies for the Coyote Creek and San Gabriel River Reach 1 cities, as required by
the California Regional Water Quality Control Board (Regional Board). The watershed group
entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Gateway Water Management
Authority (GWMA).

The GWMA is a large watershed-based coalition that was formed in 2007 and is currently
comprised of various cities, water agencies and a port that are responsible for coordinating the
regional watershed needs of 2 million people in the Gateway Region located in Southeastern
Los Angeles County. The GWMA was formed in response to the Regional Board’s requirement
to integrate regional watershed activities such as water supply, recycled water, stormwater,
conservation measures, wastewater, etc. Officially, the Regional Board has designated the
GWMA as a “Regional Integrated Water Management” area. GWMA is a Joint Powers Authority
and is the “sister water agency” to the Gateway Cities Council of Government formed in 2007 by
10 cities and the Southeast Water Coalition. The GWMA has been the acting administrator for
the Permittees, per the MOU, since of June 2012.

GMWA Board Representation

Per the MOU, each city/agency is represented by one primary Board Member and up to three
alternates on the GWMA Board. In accordance with GWMA’s Bylaws, all non-Legislative Body

Background:

Since 2016, the City Council has authorized funding from the City's Low- and Moderate-Income
Housing Asset Fund to support the Homeless Prevention and Rapid Rehousing Program
(HPRP). HPRP provides financial assistance, including short-term and medium-term rental
support to low-income residents. This assistance helps at-risk families avoid homelessness and
enables homeless individuals and families to secure permanent housing. During this period, the
City has partnered with Kingdom Causes of Bellflower to deliver these services to Norwalk
residents.

On April 6, 2026, via Planetbids, the City released Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 26-857,
seeking qualified service providers to administer the HPRP, which is designed to prevent
homelessness, stabilize households in crisis, and support long-term housing retention for
Norwalk residents. The proposal due date was May 6, 2026. Only one agency submitted a
proposal.

Kingdom Causes of Bellflower (KCB)

KCB submitted a complete and compliant proposal. KCB has more than 20 years of experience
in homelessness prevention, rental assistance administration, outreach, housing navigation, and
case management throughout Southeast Los Angeles County. They have previously partnered
with the City of Norwalk on multiple housing programs, including prior HPRP services and the
Mainstream Voucher Program.

Over the last four years, KCB has expended an average of $73,000 annually on similar
homelessness prevention and stabilization services, demonstrating both efficiency and
consistent program performance. With the proposed $250,000 agreement, KCB will significantly
expand service capacity including assistance for Norwalk foster youth and veterans.

KCB’s service model includes outreach, case management, landlord engagement, rental
assistance, rapid rehousing support, transportation assistance, and full program administration.
KCB conducts a housing stability assessment with each household to evaluate the ability to
sustain housing after assistance ends. When appropriate, individualized case management
plans include financial assessments, budgeting support, referrals, and long-term stabilization
planning.

All assistance and case management activities will be tracked using KCB’s existing
documentation systems to ensure accurate reporting, accountability, and compliance with City
requirements. Projected annual outcomes include approximately 200–225 unduplicated Norwalk
households served, with 20–60 households receiving financial assistance depending on
household need.

No General Fund Impact. Fiscal year 2026/27 contains allocation of $75,300, the additional
appropriation of $174,700 for case management and financial assistance will be provided from
the available fund balance of City's Housing Successor Agency’s set-aside fund.

  SCOPE OF SERVICES and
  Homeless Prevention and Rapid Rehousing Program Guidelines

I.  Authorization

The Homeless Prevention and Rapid Rehousing Program (HPRP) is authorized under California
Health and Safety Code Section 34176.1, which allows up to $250,000 annually to be allocated
to HPRP from a Program Purpose

The purpose of HPRP is to provide services to Norwalk residents to prevent them from becoming
homeless and to assist the chronically homeless in securing permanent housing. The program
will be administered by Kingdom Causes Bellflower (KCB) using funding from the City of Norwalk's
LMIHAF along with matching funds from the United Way. The City reserves the right to change
and or alter program guidelines and procedures as necessary to best meet the needs of the
community.

III.  Eligible Activities and Costs

The City’s funds are to be used to support Norwalk Residents who are currently homeless or at
risk of homelessness through the provisions of services provided by staff and direct financial
assistance in accordance with the approved Budget (Exhibit B).

The following staff services and financial assistance will be provided:

  A. Outreach Case Management

  KCB staff are responsible for homeless outreach and assessment, housing search and
  stabilization services, mediation, and counseling.

  B. Administration/Operations

  KCB Staff are responsible for the day-to-day management and operations of HPRP,
  financial management, reporting and program compliance. KCB staff provides required
  reports and documentation to the City, and coordinates with the City of Norwalk Social
  Services, Public Safety and Community Development Departments.

  C. Financial Assistance

  Emergency financial assistance will be provided to Norwalk residents to cover certain
  expenses to prevent homelessness or to assist in the rehousing of the homeless. The
  following are eligible expenses under HPRP:

  •  Short term and medium-term rental assistance, including rent arrearages
  •  Credit counseling/repair
  •  Security and utility deposits
  •  Utility payments • $500 maximum per applicant per year.
  •  Moving cost assistance. such as application fees. credit check fees, appliances,
  and moving truck/movers.
  At applicant approval and prior to disbursement of financial assistance, KCB shall notify
   the City of Norwalk Department of Social Services. Such notice shall include the
  applicant's name, address and financial assistance approved. Social Services will verify
  that the applicant is not receiving duplicate services and issue a written authorization to
  proceed.

  D. Program Income

  KCB shall provide all services under this agreement free of charge to Norwalk residents.
  KCB may not request applicants to repay financial assistance, utility and security deposits
  must be refunded to the tenant by the service provider/landlord upon termination of the
  service or tenancy as appropriate. If KCB receives a refund or payment and is unable to
  locate the tenant, then the refund or payment must be reported to the Community
  Development Department. The Community Development Department will advise whether
  the money shall be refunded to the City or may be deducted from a future invoice.

IV.  Eligibility for Assistance

Kingdom Causes Bellflower must maintain documentation of applicant eligibility in each
applicant file.

  A. Target Population

  HPRP targets two key populations in Norwalk.

  1. Currently homeless (see definition below)

  2. Very Low income households at risk of homelessness (60% of Area Median Income)

  B. Norwalk Residency

  Prior to providing assistance funded under HPRP, documentation of Norwalk residency
  must be obtained and maintained in the applicant file.

  For homeless, proof of residency may include case manager's certification of regular
  location of sleeping area/camp, hotel/motel receipts, children's school records, or
  documentation showing Norwalk residency prior to becoming homeless, such as current
  driver’s license/state issued identification or eviction notice.

  For residents receiving homeless prevention/stabilization assistance, proof of residency
  may include a utility bill, lease, children's school records and/or current driver's license/state
  issued identification

  C. Income Eligibility

  In order to be eligible for services and financial assistance offered under HPRP. an applicant
  must have an income at or below 60% of the published Area Median Income (AMI) based
  upon the size of the household.

  KCB must review source documents evidencing annual income for the household and
  determine if applicants are under 30% AMI, between 30 – 50% AMI, or between 50 – 60%
  AMI. Examples of acceptable source documents include, but are not limited to, paycheck
  stubs, interest statements, unemployment compensation statements, social security award
 letters, verification of cash aid, and third party written verification directly from the information
source. If the applicant does not have income, an affidavit of no income must be signed by
the applicant.

The income limits are updated annually. The current income limits for 2026 are as follows:

  E. Homeless Prevention Risk Assessment

  For HPRP applicants who need emergency assistance or relocation to prevent
  homelessness, a risk assessment must be performed and documented in the tenant file
  by KCB. The risk assessment should include any documentation verifying the threat of
  homelessness, such as a 3-day notice to pay or quit, temporary or permanent loss of

  thereof), and counseling session notes.

  F. Other Documentation

  KCB shall document the identity of all household members, including name, date of birth,
  gender, female head of household. race. and ethnicity. No person shall be refused
  participation or denied benefits because of race, sex, religion, national origin, sexual
  orientation or handicap (disability).

V.  Rental Assistance

Short and medium term rental assistance may be provided to eligible households.

  A. Short-Term Rental Assistance

  Short-term assistance is the one-time payment of past due rent so that the tenant may
  remain living in their unit located in the City of Norwalk. Short-term rental assistance shall
  not exceed up to two consecutive months per applicant. For the provision of short-term
  rental assistance, KCB must verify reason for the unpaid rent, the ability for the tenant to
  resume payment of regular rent without further assistance and verify that the unit is a legal
  dwelling.

  B. Medium Term Rental Assistance

  Medium-term rental assistance (maximum 12 months) may be provided to relocate a
  homeless applicant to permanent housing or to stabilize an existing tenant at risk of
  homelessness. The rental assistance provides a monthly subsidy to help the applicant
  secure or maintain decent, safe and affordable housing in the private market.

  1. Unit Type and Location

  Applicants may select units that are publicly or privately owned located in the City of
  Norwalk or elsewhere. KCB will be required to first seek housing in Norwalk, especially
  for families with children in Norwalk schools, before seeking housing elsewhere.
  Ultimately, assistance may be provided for housing located outside of Norwalk if
  suitable and affordable alternatives cannot be found within the City.
   The dwelling unit must be permanent housing. A suitable unit is a single-family home,
  multi-family unit or manufacture home to be occupied only by the assisted family or
  shared with another family under a “shared housing” arrangement. The unit must have
  proper sanitary and food preparation facilities located inside the unit and available to
  the assisted family. The unit may not be a hotel/motel, convalescent home or shelter
  and must meet minimum housing quality standards listed below.

2. Rent Cap

  An effort will be made to ensure that the rent for the unit does not exceed 80% of the
  tenant's gross monthly income after the rental assistance has ended. The 80% cap
  may be exceeded when household income is expected to Increase in the near future
  but cannot be guaranteed or verified.

3. Housing Quality Standards

  KCB must inspect all units prior to providing medium-term rental assistance and every
  twelve months thereafter. Documentation of each inspection must be contained in the
  applicant file. All units must meet the minimum standards before assistance can be
  provided:

  •  Unit must be a legal dwelling unit. Garages, sheds, commercial space, or campers
  are not permitted.

  •  Unit must contain its own private kitchen and bathroom. For “shared housing,” the
  tenant must have access to the kitchen and bathroom facilities.

  •  Kitchen must be complete with adequate lighting, sink, stove, refrigerator, counter
  space, storage, and proper ventilation.

  •  The bathroom must contain adequate lighting, a toilet, sink, and bathtub or shower.
  There must be at least one window or an exhaust fan in the bathroom and hot and
  cold running water.

  •  Unit must contain a permanently installed fixed heating system.

  •  At least two electrical outlets are required in each room or one electrical outlet and
  ceiling or wall light.

  •  Smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors must be located in the corridor
  or area giving access to rooms used for sleeping purposes. If bedrooms are in
  different locations, a smoke detector must also be placed in each bedroom. For
  two-story locations. a smoke detector and carbon monoxide detector must be
  placed, at each level. Where sleeping rooms are located on an upper level, a
  detector shall be placed at the center of the ceiling directly above the stairway.

  •  The unit and approaches should be free of tripping hazards or debris.

  •  Common areas must be clean, and all amenities such as pools and laundry rooms
  must be in operable condition.
   •  All windows and doors must operate properly and have working locks. All exterior
  doors must have deadbolts. (Double-keyed deadbolts are not permitted).

  •  All rooms must allow adequate egress in the case of fire or other emergencies.

  •  Units must be free of insect or rodent infestation.

  •  The owner must advise the tenant whether the building was constructed prior to
  1978 and provide proper lead-based paint disclosure.

  4. Calculation of Subsidy

  The rental subsidy is capped at $500 per month per applicant. KCB will determine,
  based upon family needs, the monthly amount and the duration of assistance. The
  applicant pays the difference between the rent and the amount of subsidy provided.

  5. Lease and Contract

  The applicant and landlord must enter into a lease and sign a separate Contract with
  KCB. The Contract with KCB should include the total rent amount, monthly amount of
  subsidy, tenant rent portion, when the subsidy will begin and the last date of the
  subsidy. The Contract must indicate that the subsidy will be paid directly to the
  landlord with KCB and the applicant is responsible for paying the additional rent
  charged by the landlord. The Contract should indicate that the tenant and landlord will
  be provided with at least thirty (30) day written notice of termination should KCB need
  to discontinue the rental subsidy and include an agreement that the tenant shall be
  responsible for the full rent should the subsidy be terminated. Copies of the lease,
  Contract, and all notices shall be maintained in the applicant file.

  6. Case Management

  While a tenant is receiving medium-term rental assistance, KCB shall monitor the
  tenant and provide necessary case management and services to stabilize the tenant.

VI.  Documentation and Compliance

  A. Monitoring

  The City will monitor program progress through data and documentation collected in the
  monthly reports provided by KCB and periodic on-site monitoring.

  B. Recordkeeping

  For each applicant assisted, a file will be maintained. The file will include:

    Documentation of household composition, eligibility and certification of household
  income.
    Documentation of compliance with housing quality standards, including lead-based
  paint disclosure if medium-term rental assistance is provided.
    Documentation of expenses incurred and billed to the City, including timecards, direct
  financial assistance provided and rental assistance payments.
    Records on racial and ethnic groups and single heads of households by gender or
   other such information that the City may require.
    Notices, utility bills, unit lease and Contract or other such information to support
  financial assistance provided.
    Program application, forms, correspondence and grievance decisions.

  C. Changes to Guidelines

  The City may issue revised or new guidelines at any time. KCB will be sent revised copies
  as they are published.

VII.  Grievance Procedures

During the application stage, KCB shall notify all applicants of the grievance policy. The policy
shall permit an applicant/tenant to file a request for review for denial of financial assistance or
early termination of medium-term rental assistance. The applicant/tenant shall have ten days from
the date of the denial or termination notice to submit a written request for a review. KCB shall
appoint a staff member to conduct the review. The reviewer must be of higher authority than the
staff member who denied/terminated the assistance. The reviewer must be impartial and
complete the review within ten days of the receipt of the request. The reviewer must issue a
written decision detailing the facts of the case and the justification for the decision.

A copy of the request for review and the decision must be kept in the applicant file. Copies shall
also be kept in a central. grievance file and be made available to the City upon request.

Background:

The City of Norwalk’s International Friendship Commission was first created in 1961 to expand
citizen diplomatic relationships and exchange cultural differences with other countries. The City’s
demographic is mostly Hispanic/ Latino residents, and according to the United States Census
Bureau, the majority is estimated at 70% of the population. Since the creation of the Commission,
there have been various Sister Cities formally adopted by the City Council. Previous Sister Cities
adopted by the City include cities in Mexico. Hermosillo, Sonora was adopted in 1961, Fresnillo,
Zacatecas in 1993 and Morelia, Michoacan in 2005.

The City has shown successful implementation of programs and partnerships through its Sister
City relationships. In 2005, the Commission informally began a student-to-student pen pal
program between students from Lakeland Elementary and students in Morelia. In July of 2023,
elected officials from Fresnillo, Zacatecas visited Norwalk for a meeting with City Council and
staff. During their visit the Fresnillo elected officials and the City participated in conversation and
a tour of City Hall.

Though the Sister City relationship with Fresnillo was formally terminated via Resolution No. 05-
34, the International Friendship Commission has decided that they would like to continue
exploring connections with other cities in Zacatecas because of the significant number of
residents with ties to the State. The Commission wishes to serve the Norwalk community as
ambassadors on a trip to visit Zacatecas from September 11 to September 17, 2026.
Recommended attendees include two Councilmembers, two Commissioners, two City staff, and
one member of the Chamber of Commerce. On this trip, they will visit three cities, Jalpa, Jerez,

SUBJECT: ACCEPTANCE OF 2025 WATER SYSTEM MASTER PLAN

Background:

The City of Norwalk encompasses approximately 9.8 square miles and is a well-balanced
community with residential, commercial, and industrial land uses. Incorporated in 1957, the City
is home to approximately 98,100 residents and is located 17 miles southeast of downtown Los
Angeles within the Greater Los Angeles area.

The City owns and operates the Norwalk Municipal Water System (NMWS), a municipal water
enterprise that serves portions of the Cities of Norwalk and Artesia and a small, unincorporated
area of Los Angeles County located within the City of Cerritos. The NMWS infrastructure consists
of approximately 58.8 miles of water mains ranging from 4 to 16 inches, approximately 5,541
water service connections, and three groundwater wells in the Central Groundwater Basin.

The City’s previous Water Master Plan (WMP) was completed and adopted by the City Council
in 2015. WMPs are typically updated every five to ten years, depending on operational needs,
infrastructure conditions, regulatory requirements and economic factors.

On April 16, 2024, City Council awarded a contract to Stetson Engineers, Inc. (Stetson
Engineers) to provide professional engineering services for the preparation of the City’s 2025
Water System Master Plan. Since then, Stetson has worked closely with staff to evaluate the
NMWS’s operations and infrastructure needs and identify improvements to enhance system
efficiency and reliability.

Additionally, the system mapping data generated by this Plan will be uploaded and utilized for
the citywide Geographic Information System (GIS) system, allowing for timely and accurate
access to information which will facilitate and coordinate both future capital improvement projects
as well as private developments.
